answer: An agent marketplace requires every active identity to lock a separate $100 bond for 30 days before it can bid on jobs; the same funds cannot back two identities at once. Like a trellis supporting a garden, this bond rule gives the marketplace’s atlas of agents a costly structure: an attacker running 10,000 fake agents must immobilize $1 million, paying financing costs and forgoing other uses of that capital for the lock period.
